callouts.description: Your car reaches the point about a second (the configured lead) before a named corner in a practice or test session, once per corner per lap; qualifying and races stay silent.
callouts.comment: The upcoming corner's bare name, spoken about a second before it in practice and test sessions — one clip, no radio frame, because at that lead the beeps would eat the whole margin. The name is the whole callout: a corner the voice has no clip for is skipped rather than half-said, and a pack that wants a lead-in puts it before the name here.
callouts.test: Harness → Corner Names → Eau Rouge (or Turn 5). In-sim: a practice session on a track with corner data, Corner names enabled; the name plays on the approach to each corner.

callouts.description: Your car takes damage that keeps the repair indicator lit for three seconds running, and again only after a repair has cleared it.
callouts.comment: The car has picked up damage the crew can repair — spoken once when iRacing first flags a mandatory or optional repair. A meatball flag carries the same news with more authority and outranks this line.
callouts.test: Harness → Damage → Damage Detected. In-sim: hit a wall or another car hard enough for the repair indicator to light in the black box.

callouts.description: iRacing shows you the black flag on its own, in any session; when it comes together with a disqualification the disqualify line speaks instead.
callouts.comment: A black flag has been issued — the driver has a penalty to serve within three laps.
callouts.test: Harness → Flags → Black. In-sim: speed in the pit lane, or ignore a furled black flag; a race admin can also issue one (!black).

callouts.description: A faster car is closing to lap you and iRacing shows you the blue flag, in any session; a blue shown together with the green at a start is ignored.
callouts.comment: A faster car is about to lap the driver — asks for mirrors and a clean pass.
callouts.test: Harness → Flags → Blue. In-sim: get shown the blue flag as a lapping car closes in.

callouts.description: The full-course caution is shown waving to the field, in any session; a repeat inside thirty seconds stays silent.
callouts.comment: The caution is out and waving — slow down and close up safely. Repeats at most once per 30 seconds.
callouts.test: Harness → Flags → Caution Waving. In-sim: the caution comes out on an oval as the field bunches up.

callouts.description: You take the checkered flag: at your own crossing of the line in qualifying and a race (the flag flies for the field before that), or the moment the session ends in practice.
callouts.comment: The checkered flag — the session is over. The wording follows session.type (the well-done only after a race); an unknown session type takes the race line.
callouts.test: Harness → Flags → Checkered, after choosing a session preset. In-sim: take the checkered flag at the end of any session.

callouts.description: The crossed flags come out at the halfway point of a race while you are live in the car; never in practice or qualifying, and never after the checkered.
callouts.comment: Crossed flags — the halfway point of the race. Race-only, while the driver is live in the car.
callouts.test: Harness → Flags → Crossed, with the race session preset and the hot-lap telemetry preset. In-sim: reach the halfway point of an oval race.

callouts.description: iRacing shows the debris flag for something lying on the track ahead, in any session; only the raise speaks, never the clear.
callouts.comment: A debris flag — something is on the track ahead; asks the driver to be careful.
callouts.test: Harness → Flags → Debris. In-sim: the debris flag after an incident leaves parts on the track.

callouts.description: iRacing disqualifies you and shows the disqualify flag — the incident limit, or a race admin — in any session; a black flag shown alongside it stays silent.
callouts.comment: The driver has been disqualified — pull off the track.
callouts.test: Harness → Flags → Disqualify. In-sim: exceed the session's incident limit, or a race admin disqualifies you (!dq).

callouts.description: iRacing shows the flag that disqualifies you and invalidates your scoring at the same time, in any session.
callouts.comment: The driver has been disqualified and their scoring invalidated — DQ, scoring's off.
callouts.test: Harness → Flags → DQ — Scoring Invalid. In-sim: a disqualification that also invalidates scoring (rare; the harness is the practical route).

callouts.description: Five laps remain in a race and iRacing raises the five-to-go flag while you are live in the car; never after the checkered or outside a race.
callouts.comment: Five laps to go. Race-only, live in the car.
callouts.test: Harness → Flags → Five to Go, with the race session preset and the hot-lap telemetry preset. In-sim: five laps remaining in an oval race.

callouts.description: The furled black flag has stayed up on your car for a full second — a warning for time gained off track, not the half-second flicker of a brief excursion — in any session.
callouts.comment: The furled black flag — the driver gained time and must give it back. Spoken only while the flag is still shown at speak time, so a warning withdrawn while this waited behind a longer line stays silent.
callouts.test: Harness → Flags → Furled. In-sim: cut a corner and gain time; the furled flag shows until the time is given back.

callouts.description: The furled black flag comes down off your car after it was called, in any session, with no black flag or disqualification taking its place at that moment.
callouts.comment: The furled warning has been withdrawn after the driver gave the time back. Only follows a furled line that was actually spoken, and never plays when the warning escalated to a real black flag instead.
callouts.test: Harness → Flags → Furled, then Harness → Flags → Furled Cleared. In-sim: give the time back after a furled black flag.

callouts.description: The green flag comes out at the start of a practice or qualifying session or at a race restart; the initial race start belongs to the start lights and stays silent here.
callouts.comment: The green flag at the start of a session or a restart. The wording differs per session type (practice, qualifying, race), so it branches on session.type; an unknown session type takes the race line.
callouts.test: Harness → Flags → Green, after choosing a session preset (practice, qualifying or race). In-sim: the green at the start of any session, or at a race restart.

callouts.description: iRacing holds the green on the final pace lap of a rolling start or restart, as the pace car pulls in, while you are live in the car; never on a standing-start grid.
callouts.comment: The pace car is pulling in and the green is imminent — get ready to launch. Rolling starts and restarts only; a standing-start grid is the start lights' business.
callouts.test: Harness → Flags → Green Held, with the race session preset and the hot-lap telemetry preset. In-sim: the final pace lap of a rolling start or restart, once the pace car peels off.

callouts.description: Your car takes enough damage that iRacing orders it to the pits and shows you the meatball flag, in any session.
callouts.comment: The meatball flag — mandatory repairs, the driver must pit. Cuts any other line in flight and is never dropped.
callouts.test: Harness → Flags → Meatball. In-sim: take enough damage that iRacing orders you in for repairs.

callouts.description: The pace car crosses the start/finish line to complete the first pace lap of a two-lap rolling start while the green is still held, with you live in the car.
callouts.comment: One more pace lap before the green on a rolling start — keep the spacing tidy and warm the tires. Race-only, live in the car.
callouts.test: Harness → Flags → One Pace Lap to Go, with the race session preset and the hot-lap telemetry preset. In-sim: the second-to-last pace lap of a rolling start.

callouts.description: A red flag is thrown and the session is halted, in any session type.
callouts.comment: The red flag — the session is stopped; tells the driver to slow down and drive carefully back to the pits.
callouts.test: Harness → Flags → Red. In-sim: a red flag in a hosted or league session.

callouts.description: Ten laps remain in a race and iRacing raises the ten-to-go flag while you are live in the car; never after the checkered or outside a race.
callouts.comment: Ten laps to go. Race-only, live in the car.
callouts.test: Harness → Flags → Ten to Go, with the race session preset and the hot-lap telemetry preset. In-sim: ten laps remaining in an oval race.

callouts.description: iRacing raises the white flag: in a race while the leader is still approaching the line for the final lap, in practice or qualifying as you begin your own last lap.
callouts.comment: The white flag — the leader's final lap in a race, or the last lap of a practice or qualifying session; the wording follows session.type, and an unknown session type takes the race line.
callouts.test: Harness → Flags → White, after choosing a session preset. In-sim: the white flag comes out on the leader's final lap (race) or on your own last lap (practice, qualifying).

callouts.description: You cross the start/finish line with the white flag flying in a race and begin your own final lap, once per white flag; a crossing that lands while the heads-up is still playing is skipped.
callouts.comment: The driver has crossed the line under the white flag and started their own last lap — give it everything. Race-only; stage two of the white-flag call.
callouts.test: Harness → Flags → White — Last Lap Started, with the race session preset. In-sim: cross start/finish while the white flag flies in a race.

callouts.description: The overall race leader starts the final lap, judged from lap counting, while you are not the leader and have no white flag of your own yet; once per race.
callouts.comment: The overall leader has started their final lap while the driver is still some way behind — a heads-up that the race is about to end.
callouts.test: Harness → Flags → Leader's final lap, with the race session preset. In-sim: in a race, let the leader take the white flag while you are a lap or more down.

callouts.description: Every yellow and caution flag has been down for three seconds straight after a yellow, so the all-clear is confirmed rather than a gap between zones.
callouts.comment: The yellow has been withdrawn — a short all-clear, replayed after a busier line finishes rather than dropped.
callouts.test: Harness → Flags → Yellow Cleared. In-sim: clear the local yellow sector, or the caution ends and racing resumes.

callouts.description: iRacing shows you a standing (not waving) full-course caution, putting the whole field under yellow, in any session.
callouts.comment: A full-course yellow is out — tells the driver the pace car is being deployed and to close up safely.
callouts.test: Harness → Flags → Yellow (full). In-sim: a full-course caution in an oval race (the pace car is deployed).

callouts.description: iRacing shows you a standing (not waving) local yellow for an incident in the sector ahead, in any session.
callouts.comment: A local yellow is shown for an incident ahead — one short warning to slow down and mind the stopped cars. A full-course yellow takes the flag-yellow-full line instead.
callouts.test: Harness → Flags → Yellow (local). In-sim: drive up to a stopped or spun car in a local yellow sector.

callouts.description: You enter the zone of a fresh incident and iRacing shows you the waving local yellow, in any session; a later pass through the same zone re-raises it, at most once per thirty seconds.
callouts.comment: A waving yellow — a fresh incident right ahead, more urgent than the standing yellow. Repeats at most once per 30 seconds while the incident persists.
callouts.test: Harness → Flags → Yellow Waving. In-sim: approach a sector where a car has just crashed or spun.

callouts.description: Mid-lap in a race, live in the car, your fuel estimate first drops to one more full lap — once per stint, and never once the tank covers the rest of the race.
callouts.comment: One lap of fuel left — critical: it cuts whatever is playing, because the next crossing is the box call.
callouts.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Fuel → 1 lap of fuel left. In-sim: the estimate falls through one.

callouts.description: Mid-lap in a race, live in the car, your fuel estimate first drops to ten more full laps — once per stint, and never once the tank covers the rest of the race.
callouts.comment: The tank is estimated to cover ten more laps — ordinary commentary, spoken once when the estimate first drops through ten. A fresher count replaces a stale one still playing.
callouts.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Fuel → 10 laps of fuel left. In-sim: run a stint until the laps-of-fuel estimate falls through ten.

callouts.description: Mid-lap in a race, live in the car, your fuel estimate first drops to two more full laps — once per stint, and never once the tank covers the rest of the race.
callouts.comment: Two laps of fuel left — the second warning, same weight as the flags.
callouts.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Fuel → 2 laps of fuel left. In-sim: the estimate falls through two.

callouts.description: Mid-lap in a race, live in the car, your fuel estimate first drops to three more full laps — once per stint, and never once the tank covers the rest of the race.
callouts.comment: Three laps of fuel left — a warning at the flags' weight, so it takes the bus from ordinary chatter and is replayed rather than dropped behind a flag.
callouts.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Fuel → 3 laps of fuel left. In-sim: the estimate falls through three.

callouts.description: Mid-lap in a race, live in the car, your fuel estimate first drops to four more full laps — once per stint, and never once the tank covers the rest of the race.
callouts.comment: Four laps of fuel left — the last of the ordinary-commentary counts before the warnings start.
callouts.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Fuel → 4 laps of fuel left. In-sim: the estimate falls through four.

callouts.description: Mid-lap in a race, live in the car, your fuel estimate first drops to five more full laps — once per stint, and never once the tank covers the rest of the race.
callouts.comment: Five laps of fuel left — ordinary commentary at the lap cadence.
callouts.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Fuel → 5 laps of fuel left. In-sim: the estimate falls through five.

callouts.description: Mid-lap in a race, live in the car, your fuel estimate first drops to six more full laps — once per stint, and never once the tank covers the rest of the race.
callouts.comment: Six laps of fuel left — ordinary commentary at the lap cadence.
callouts.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Fuel → 6 laps of fuel left. In-sim: the estimate falls through six.

callouts.description: Mid-lap in a race, live in the car, your fuel estimate first drops to seven more full laps — once per stint, and never once the tank covers the rest of the race.
callouts.comment: Seven laps of fuel left — ordinary commentary at the lap cadence.
callouts.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Fuel → 7 laps of fuel left. In-sim: the estimate falls through seven.

callouts.description: Mid-lap in a race, live in the car, your fuel estimate first drops to eight more full laps — once per stint, and never once the tank covers the rest of the race.
callouts.comment: Eight laps of fuel left — ordinary commentary at the lap cadence.
callouts.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Fuel → 8 laps of fuel left. In-sim: the estimate falls through eight.

callouts.description: Mid-lap in a race, live in the car, your fuel estimate first drops to nine more full laps — once per stint, and never once the tank covers the rest of the race.
callouts.comment: Nine laps of fuel left — ordinary commentary at the lap cadence.
callouts.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Fuel → 9 laps of fuel left. In-sim: the estimate falls through nine.

callouts.description: Mid-lap in a race, live in the car, your fuel estimate first drops below one more full lap — once per stint, and never once the tank covers the rest of the race.
callouts.comment: The tank will not cover another full lap — box this lap for fuel. Critical and interrupting: nothing in flight is worth more than this instruction.
callouts.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Fuel → Box this lap. In-sim: keep running until the estimate falls below one lap.

callouts.description: Inside the last ten laps of a race, live in the car, the mid-lap fuel estimate shows the tank covering the rest of the race with a full lap in hand — once per stint.
callouts.comment: Good news inside the last ten laps: the tank covers the rest of the race with a lap in hand. Spoken once per stint, at ordinary weight — good news never needs to cut anything.
callouts.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Fuel → Enough fuel to finish. In-sim: with ten or fewer laps to go in a race, carry more fuel than the remaining distance needs.

callouts.description: The live gap to the car ahead or behind you in your class first drops under your alert threshold in a race, in a clean moment with no car alongside and no recent incident.
callouts.comment: The gap to a standings neighbor first dropped under the driver's alert threshold — we have caught the car ahead, or the car behind is right with us — then the live gap through the same gap-readout fragment. Shares the trend line's cooldown.
callouts.test: Harness → Gaps → Caught the car ahead (threshold) or Car behind within threshold, with a live gap for the seconds clause. In-sim: close to within the configured gap threshold of the car ahead.

callouts.description: The gap to the car ahead or behind you in your class turns — closing fast enough to reach it within eight laps, or opening into a breakaway — in a race, with no car alongside and no recent incident.
callouts.comment: The gap to a standings neighbor has turned: we are gaining on the car ahead, it is pulling away, the car behind is gaining, or we are dropping it. The line is chosen by side and direction; the live gap readout follows through the gap-readout fragment. Both gap lines share one cooldown (30 s by default), so a second one inside it stays silent.
callouts.test: Harness → Gaps → Trend: closing on car ahead, Trend: car ahead pulling away, Trend: car behind gaining or Trend: dropping the car behind — the seconds clause needs a live gap, so drive the harness session with cars around you. In-sim: race with a car a few seconds ahead and close on it lap after lap.

callouts.description: You collide heavily with another car in any session outside the pits — the worst outcome a crash sequence can reach, called once the sequence has settled.
callouts.comment: A heavy collision with another car: the type line, then the points it cost as an optional whole clause — four on pavement, two on dirt, whatever the sim scored, and nothing for a count the voice cannot say.
callouts.test: Harness → Incidents → Collision — Car (4x), Collision — Car (2x, dirt) or Collision — Car (escalated). In-sim: a hard collision with another car.

callouts.description: You hit a wall or a trackside object hard enough for iRacing to score it as a collision, in any session outside the pits, with no car collision following within a second or two.
callouts.comment: A hard hit on the wall or scenery: the type line, then the points it cost as an optional whole clause.
callouts.test: Harness → Incidents → Collision — Wall (2x). In-sim: hit a wall hard.

callouts.description: You make light contact with another car in any session outside the pits, with no heavier collision following within a second or two.
callouts.comment: Light contact with another car: the type line, then the points it cost as an optional whole clause — nothing when the rub cost none.
callouts.test: Harness → Incidents → Contact — Car (0x). In-sim: rub doors with another car.

callouts.description: You brush a wall or a trackside object lightly in any session outside the pits, with no harder hit following within a second or two.
callouts.comment: Light contact with the wall or scenery: the type line, then the points it cost as a separate clause. The count is optional because it is a whole sentence of its own — a light touch worth no points, or a count the voice has no clip for, leaves the type line standing on its own.
callouts.test: Harness → Incidents → Contact — Wall (0x) (the type line alone) or Collision — Wall (2x) for a count. In-sim: brush a wall lightly.

callouts.description: You run all four wheels off the track in any session outside the pits, and nothing worse follows within a second or two; on a timed qualifying lap the lap-invalidated line speaks first.
callouts.comment: The driver ran off track — a short coaching line about track limits, with no point count (the type has none worth stating). A faster, worse incident in the same crash replaces this line mid-sentence.
callouts.test: Harness → Incidents → Off Track (1x). In-sim: put four wheels off in any session.

callouts.description: You lose control of the car — a spin — in any session outside the pits, and nothing worse follows within a second or two.
callouts.comment: The driver lost control of the car (a spin) — a calm-down line, no point count.
callouts.test: Harness → Incidents → Out of Control (2x). In-sim: spin the car.

callouts.description: You cross the line with a new session-best lap, or your first valid lap of the session, in any session — except on the final lap of a race, where the result speaks instead.
callouts.comment: A new session-best lap, or the driver's first valid lap: the intro (best-lap-yet or first-good-lap), then the time as minute, seconds and tenths. The minute is a hard if here — a terse pack may write it as optional, since the assumed minute is understood, but only where that minute is 1; every other component is required, because a time missing its seconds is not a time.
callouts.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Lap Time → Best Lap 1:03.4 (Best Lap 0:34.8 for a lap without the minute, First Valid Lap 2:07.0 for the other intro). In-sim: set a personal best in any session, or complete the first clean lap of a session.

callouts.description: You switch the pit limiter off while still between the pit cones and moving at more than a crawl, in a car that has one.
callouts.comment: The limiter was switched off while the car is still between the pit cones — turn it back on.
callouts.test: Harness → Pit Limiter → Limiter dropped. In-sim: on a car with a pit limiter, disengage it while still on pit road.

callouts.description: You drive onto pit road, or pull away from your stall, with the pit limiter off, and it is still off two and a half seconds later, in a car that has one.
callouts.comment: The car is on pit road without its limiter engaged, a couple of seconds after the pit-entry reminder went unheeded — an escalation, not a duplicate. The whole body is behind limiter.stillMissingOnPitRoad, so a driver who engaged the limiter in the meantime hears nothing.
callouts.test: Harness → Pit Limiter → Limiter off on pit road (fires about 2.5 s later). In-sim: on a car with a pit limiter, enter pit road without engaging it and keep it off.

callouts.description: About a second and a half after you leave pit road, the pit limiter is still switched on, in a car that has one.
callouts.comment: The pit limiter is still on about a second and a half after the car left pit road — the driver forgot to switch it off. The whole body is behind limiter.stillEngagedOffPitRoad: the line waits behind busier traffic rather than being dropped, so it re-checks live telemetry when it comes to speak and says nothing (no radio frame either) once the limiter is off.
callouts.test: Harness → Pit Limiter → Limiter on out on track (fires about 1.5 s later). In-sim: on a car with a pit limiter, leave pit road with the limiter still engaged.

callouts.description: You go over the pit speed limit on pit road in a car that has a pit limiter, no more than once every five seconds.
callouts.comment: The car is over the pit speed limit on a car that has a limiter — the fix is to press the button, which is why this line is separate from the no-limiter one.
callouts.test: Harness → Pit Limiter → Speeding (limiter car). In-sim: on a car with a pit limiter, exceed the pit speed limit on pit road.

callouts.description: You drive onto pit road in a car that has no pit limiter.
callouts.comment: Pit entry on a car with no limiter: a reminder to mind the limit, then the limit itself — intro, number, unit — as one optional clause. The number is the whole point of the clause and a fragment of its sentence, so a limit the voice has no clip for drops the clause entirely rather than speaking the intro into silence; the reminder still stands alone as a complete sentence.
callouts.test: Harness → No Pit Limiter → Pit entry reminder, after Harness → Session Start → Fire Session Start with the Pit speed limit set (the limit clause reads that snapshot; without one only the reminder plays). In-sim: on a car without a pit limiter, enter pit road.

callouts.description: You go over the pit speed limit on pit road in a car that has no pit limiter, no more than once every five seconds.
callouts.comment: Over the pit speed limit on a car that has NO pit limiter — the fix is to lift, so this line must never mention a limiter. The mirror of limiter-speeding; exactly one of the two speaks to any car.
callouts.test: Harness → No Pit Limiter → Speeding (no limiter). In-sim: on a car without a pit limiter, exceed the pit speed limit on pit road.

callouts.description: A car in your class up to three places ahead of you on the same lap is black-flagged in a race, between the green and the checkered flag.
callouts.comment: A car up to three places ahead in the standings has been black-flagged, named by its position — car-in, the number, the black tail. The number is part of the sentence.
callouts.test: Harness → Opponent Flags → P5 ahead: black flag. In-sim: the car one place ahead of you is black-flagged during a race.

callouts.description: The car in your class one place behind you on the same lap is black-flagged in a race, between the green and the checkered flag.
callouts.comment: The car directly behind in the standings has been black-flagged — the pressure from behind should ease.
callouts.test: Harness → Opponent Flags → Behind: black flag. In-sim: the car one place behind you is black-flagged during a race.

callouts.description: A car less than about ten seconds ahead of you on the road, of any class or lap and not in the pits, is black-flagged in a race, between the green and the checkered flag.
callouts.comment: A car the driver is closing on along the track has been black-flagged — a safety-weighted heads-up.
callouts.test: Harness → Opponent Flags → Track ahead: black flag. In-sim: close in on a black-flagged car ahead on the road.

callouts.description: A car in your class up to three places ahead of you on the same lap is disqualified in a race, between the green and the checkered flag.
callouts.comment: A car up to three places ahead in the standings has been disqualified, named by its position — car-in, the number, the disqualified tail. The number is part of the sentence.
callouts.test: Harness → Opponent Flags → P5 ahead: DQ. In-sim: the car one place ahead of you is disqualified during a race.

callouts.description: The car in your class one place behind you on the same lap is disqualified in a race, between the green and the checkered flag.
callouts.comment: The car directly behind in the standings has been disqualified.
callouts.test: Harness → Opponent Flags → Behind: DQ. In-sim: the car one place behind you is disqualified during a race.

callouts.description: A car less than about ten seconds ahead of you on the road, of any class or lap and not in the pits, is disqualified in a race, between the green and the checkered flag.
callouts.comment: A car the driver is closing on along the track has been disqualified and may pull off — a safety-weighted heads-up.
callouts.test: Harness → Opponent Flags → Track ahead: DQ. In-sim: close in on a disqualified car ahead on the road.

callouts.description: A car in your class up to three places ahead of you on the same lap is shown a furled black flag in a race, between the green and the checkered flag.
callouts.comment: A car up to three places ahead in the standings has been shown a furled black flag, named by its position: the car-in lead-in (the opponent-pit family's clip, reused because the words are the same), the number, then the furled tail. The number is part of the sentence — a position the voice cannot say skips the whole line. Every opponent-flag line queues behind a busier one rather than cutting it, because each describes a different car.
callouts.test: Harness → Opponent Flags → P5 ahead: furled. In-sim: the car one place ahead of you picks up a furled black flag during a race.

callouts.description: The car in your class one place behind you on the same lap is shown a furled black flag in a race, between the green and the checkered flag.
callouts.comment: The car directly behind in the standings has been shown a furled black flag.
callouts.test: Harness → Opponent Flags → Behind: furled. In-sim: the car one place behind you picks up a furled black flag during a race.

callouts.description: A car less than about ten seconds ahead of you on the road, of any class or lap and not in the pits, is shown a furled black flag in a race, between the green and the checkered flag.
callouts.comment: A car the driver is closing on along the track carries a furled black flag — a safety-weighted heads-up, since a penalised car may be slow.
callouts.test: Harness → Opponent Flags → Track ahead: furled. In-sim: close in on a car ahead on the road that has a furled black flag.

callouts.description: A car in your class up to three places ahead of you on the same lap is shown the meatball flag in a race, between the green and the checkered flag.
callouts.comment: A car up to three places ahead in the standings has the meatball (repair) flag, named by its position — car-in, the number, the meatball tail. The number is part of the sentence.
callouts.test: Harness → Opponent Flags → P5 ahead: meatball. In-sim: the car one place ahead of you is shown the meatball flag during a race.

callouts.description: The car in your class one place behind you on the same lap is shown the meatball flag in a race, between the green and the checkered flag.
callouts.comment: The car directly behind in the standings has the meatball flag and will be coming in for repairs.
callouts.test: Harness → Opponent Flags → Behind: meatball. In-sim: the car one place behind you is shown the meatball flag during a race.

callouts.description: A car less than about ten seconds ahead of you on the road, of any class or lap and not in the pits, is shown the meatball flag in a race, between the green and the checkered flag.
callouts.comment: A car the driver is closing on along the track has the meatball flag — a damaged car that could be slow, so a safety-weighted warning.
callouts.test: Harness → Opponent Flags → Track ahead: meatball. In-sim: close in on a car ahead on the road that is showing the meatball flag.

callouts.description: A third car near you picks up a penalty flag within twelve seconds of the first two in a race, and further flagged cars stay uncalled until things go quiet.
callouts.comment: Several cars around the driver picked up penalty flags in the same burst — the aggregate tail after the individual lines. It only ever describes flags the user opted into, because the per-flag opt-ins are applied before anything reaches the aggregate.
callouts.test: Harness → Opponent Flags → Several cars flagged. In-sim: a multi-car incident that hands penalties to several cars near you at once.

callouts.description: The car one place ahead of you in your class, on the same lap, heads into the pits during a race, between the green and the checkered flag.
callouts.comment: The car directly ahead in the standings has entered the pits.
callouts.test: Harness → Opponent Pit → Car ahead pitting. In-sim: the car one place ahead of you pits during a race.

callouts.description: The car one place behind you in your class, on the same lap, heads into the pits during a race, between the green and the checkered flag.
callouts.comment: The car directly behind in the standings has entered the pits.
callouts.test: Harness → Opponent Pit → Car behind pitting. In-sim: the car one place behind you pits during a race.

callouts.description: The race leader, or your class leader in a multi-class race, heads into the pits during a race, between the green and the checkered flag.
callouts.comment: The race leader has entered the pits — strategic news, spoken as one line. Every opponent-pit line queues behind a busier one rather than cutting it, because each describes a different car.
callouts.test: Harness → Opponent Pit → Leader pitting. In-sim: a race where the leader pits while you are on track.

callouts.description: A car two places ahead of or behind you in your class, on the same lap, heads into the pits during a race, between the green and the checkered flag.
callouts.comment: A car within two places of the driver has entered the pits, named by its position: the car-in lead-in, the number, the is-pitting tail. The number is read live at speak time and is part of the sentence — a position the voice cannot say skips the whole line, never the middle of it.
callouts.test: Harness → Opponent Pit → P7 pitting (±2). In-sim: a car two places ahead or behind you pits during a race.

callouts.description: A third car around you heads into the pits within twelve seconds of the first two in a race, and further stops stay uncalled until the burst has passed.
callouts.comment: Several cars pitted in the same burst — the aggregate tail after the individual lines, so a pit train is not narrated car by car.
callouts.test: Harness → Opponent Pit → Several cars pitting. In-sim: a pit window opens and a group of cars dives in together.

callouts.description: You gain a place in a race and hold it a few seconds in a clean moment — always for a podium place, about one in three otherwise, and in a single-class race never when the car ahead simply retired.
callouts.comment: The reaction to a gained overtake, one line chosen by what the pass earned: the lead (overall, or in class in a multi-class race), second or third place — each of those states the position itself, so no readout follows — or the plain "Nice pass" for anything else, which the separate position readout then completes. A podium pass always reacts; any other pass reacts about one time in three, and a place gained because a car ahead retired never does.
callouts.test: Harness → Overtakes → Gained — now P5 (nice pass), Gained the lead (P2 → P1), Gained — multi-class (class P3 → P2), Gained — P3 → P2 (podium line), Gained — P4 → P3 (podium line); Gained — retirement (readout only) stays silent here. In-sim: pass a car cleanly in a race.

callouts.description: You gain a place below the podium (a podium gain has its own reaction line) in a running race and hold it a few seconds in a clean moment, with no other position readout in the last twenty seconds.
callouts.comment: The position readout after a gained overtake — "We're currently", then the live position — played once the reaction line has finished. It is skipped for a podium gain, whose reaction line already states the place, and never doubles a position announced by another line in the last 20 seconds. The lead-in is an optional clause: a second readout within 30 seconds that moved at most one place says the bare number ("P four"), which is a complete, true statement on its own; a script that always wants the lead-in drops the optional.
callouts.test: Harness: mute — the Overtakes buttons fire the reaction but the harness has no live position, so this readout has nothing to say there. In-sim: pass a car in a race outside the top three; the reaction (when it rolls) is followed by the current position, and a second pass within half a minute reads the bare number.

callouts.description: You lose a place in a race and the drop holds for a few seconds in a clean moment — always when it costs you a podium place, about one time in three otherwise.
callouts.comment: The reaction to a lost place: "Come on, <name>." in the driver's chosen name, then "Don't give up positions like that." The opener is a complete sentence of its own and is optional — a voice without a clip for the chosen name skips it and the line still plays. A lost podium place always reacts; any other loss about one time in three.
callouts.test: Harness → Overtakes → Lost — now P5. In-sim: get passed in a race.

callouts.description: You lose a place in a running race and the drop holds a few seconds, with no car alongside, not on pit road, no incident in the last ten seconds and no other position readout in the last twenty.
callouts.comment: The position readout after a lost place — the same lead-in and live number as the gained readout, under the same 20-second no-double rule and the same optional lead-in.
callouts.test: Harness: mute — the Overtakes → Lost — now P5 button fires the reaction but the harness has no live position for this readout. In-sim: get passed in a race; the come-on line (when it rolls) is followed by the current position.

callouts.description: On pit road heading for your own box, you close to 120 meters from it.
callouts.comment: The pit-box count-in, 120 m out — the first of six marks spoken about a second apart on the approach to the driver's own box. Terse by design: the engine puts no radio frame around any mark, and a mark that cannot take the bus is dropped rather than replayed late.
callouts.test: Harness → Pit Box → Five (120 m). In-sim: drive down pit road toward your own stall; the marks fire at 120, 100, 80, 60, 40 and 20 m.

callouts.description: On pit road heading for your own box, you close to 100 meters from it.
callouts.comment: The count-in's second mark, 100 m out.
callouts.test: Harness → Pit Box → Four (100 m). In-sim: as for the five mark, 100 m from the stall.

callouts.description: On pit road heading for your own box, you close to 40 meters from it.
callouts.comment: The count-in's fifth mark, 40 m out.
callouts.test: Harness → Pit Box → One (40 m). In-sim: as for the five mark, 40 m from the stall.

callouts.description: On pit road heading for your own box, you close to 20 meters from it.
callouts.comment: The last mark, 20 m out — the cue to stop in the box.
callouts.test: Harness → Pit Box → Pit now (20 m). In-sim: as for the five mark, 20 m from the stall.

callouts.description: On pit road heading for your own box, you close to 80 meters from it.
callouts.comment: The count-in's third mark, 80 m out.
callouts.test: Harness → Pit Box → Three (80 m). In-sim: as for the five mark, 80 m from the stall.

callouts.description: On pit road heading for your own box, you close to 60 meters from it.
callouts.comment: The count-in's fourth mark, 60 m out.
callouts.test: Harness → Pit Box → Two (60 m). In-sim: as for the five mark, 60 m from the stall.

callouts.description: You reach the pit-lane approach zone under your own power, change the queued service while still on pit road, or have been in the pre-start formation for about five seconds.
callouts.comment: Reads back the queued pit service as the car enters the pit lane, and again — without the opener — after the driver changes the queue while still on pit road. A limiter reminder leads on the initial entry when the car has one and it is off; nothing queued collapses the whole recap to the empty-fallback line.
callouts.test: Harness → Pit Service Readback → Fire Readback, with Reason set to entry (entry-refire for the mid-lane replay) after setting a service snapshot with the Fuel Queued, Tires LF/RF/LR/RR (or the All / Fronts / Rears / Lefts / Rights / None presets), Compound, Fast Repair Queued / Available and Windshield Queued controls; leave Limiter Engaged unchecked for the pre-opener, and set damage on the Engine Warnings panel for the fast-repair slot. In-sim: queue fuel and two tires, then enter the pit lane.

callouts.description: You leave pit road and stay out for about four and a half seconds without turning back in.
callouts.comment: Confirms the queued pit service a few seconds after the car leaves the pit lane — the same recap under a "to confirm" opener, which stays even when nothing is queued so the empty-fallback line still reads as a confirmation.
callouts.test: Harness → Pit Service Readback → Fire Readback, with Reason set to exit after setting a service snapshot with the same controls. In-sim: queue a service, drive through the pits and out; the confirmation follows the pit-lane exit.

callouts.description: You stop across your box at an angle the crew cannot work at.
callouts.comment: The car is parked at an angle the crew cannot work at — the first, full correction.
callouts.test: Harness → Pit Status → Bad Angle. In-sim: stop in the box with the car turned across it.

callouts.description: You stay parked across your box at a bad angle after the first correction, about every two seconds while the car is at rest.
callouts.comment: The repeat nag for a bad angle — the whole body behind its live re-check, as for too far left.
callouts.test: Harness → Pit Status → Still Bad Angle, after Bad Angle. In-sim: park across the box and stay put.

callouts.description: You stop in your pit box with damage the crew cannot repair.
callouts.comment: The crew cannot repair the damage this stop — the car is done.
callouts.test: Harness → Pit Status → Can't Fix That. In-sim: pit with damage beyond what a pit stop can repair.

callouts.description: The crew completes every queued service on your car in the pit box.
callouts.comment: The service is finished and the car is ready to leave the box.
callouts.test: Harness → Pit Status → Complete. In-sim: wait out the queued service in the box; the line plays as the crew finishes.

callouts.description: You are stopped in your pit box and the crew begins working on the car.
callouts.comment: The crew has started working on the car. One of eight pit-status lines, each spoken once when iRacing's pit-service status changes to it; a newer status replaces the one still playing.
callouts.test: Harness → Pit Status → In Progress. In-sim: stop in the box with a service queued; the line plays as the crew starts.

callouts.description: You stop short of your box marks, too far back for the crew to work on the car.
callouts.comment: The car stopped short of the box — the first, full correction.
callouts.test: Harness → Pit Status → Too Far Back. In-sim: stop before your box marks.

callouts.description: You stay parked short of your box marks after the first correction, about every two seconds while the car is at rest.
callouts.comment: The repeat nag for too far back — the whole body behind its live re-check, as for too far left.
callouts.test: Harness → Pit Status → Still Too Far Back, after Too Far Back. In-sim: stop short of the box and stay put.

callouts.description: You overshoot your box marks and stop too far forward for the crew to work on the car.
callouts.comment: The car overshot the box — the first, full correction.
callouts.test: Harness → Pit Status → Too Far Forward. In-sim: stop past your box marks.

callouts.description: You stay parked past your box marks after the first correction, about every two seconds while the car is at rest.
callouts.comment: The repeat nag for too far forward — the whole body behind its live re-check, as for too far left.
callouts.test: Harness → Pit Status → Still Too Far Forward, after Too Far Forward. In-sim: overshoot the box and stay put.

callouts.description: You stop in the pit lane too far left of your box for the crew to work on the car.
callouts.comment: The car stopped too far left of the box for the crew to work — the first, full correction; the terse repeat nag takes over while the error persists.
callouts.test: Harness → Pit Status → Too Far Left. In-sim: stop in the pit lane left of your box marks.

callouts.description: You stay parked too far left of your box after the first correction, about every two seconds while the car is at rest.
callouts.comment: The terse nag that repeats every couple of seconds while the car sits too far left after the full correction. The whole body is behind pitStatus.stillTooFarLeft: a nag that waited behind a longer line re-checks the live status when it comes to speak and says nothing once the driver has corrected — and nothing means no radio frame either, which is the intended silence rather than a bare beep.
callouts.test: Harness → Pit Status → Still Too Far Left, after Too Far Left. In-sim: stop left of the box and stay put; the nag repeats about every two seconds.

callouts.description: You stop in the pit lane too far right of your box for the crew to work on the car.
callouts.comment: The car stopped too far right of the box — the first, full correction.
callouts.test: Harness → Pit Status → Too Far Right. In-sim: stop in the pit lane right of your box marks.

callouts.description: You stay parked too far right of your box after the first correction, about every two seconds while the car is at rest.
callouts.comment: The repeat nag for too far right — the whole body behind its live re-check, as for too far left.
callouts.test: Harness → Pit Status → Still Too Far Right, after Too Far Right. In-sim: stop right of the box and stay put.

callouts.description: Pit road switches from open to closed while you are in a race session.
callouts.comment: Pit road has closed for the driver — the counterpart line. A rapid open/closed flurry replaces the stale in-flight line rather than stacking both.
callouts.test: Harness → Pit Window → Pits closed. In-sim: the pits close in a race — when the caution comes out on an oval, or in the final laps.

callouts.description: Pit road switches from closed to open while you are in a race session.
callouts.comment: Pit road has opened for the driver — one line, above ordinary chatter but below a flag, replayed after a busier line finishes rather than dropped because the window matters to strategy.
callouts.test: Harness → Pit Window → Pits opened. In-sim: the pits open in a race — after the field takes the green, or when a caution's pit window opens.

callouts.description: You finish a qualifying or race lap in a new position, or your first timed lap; a held place counts only on a non-best qualifying lap; in a race, no position readout in the past twenty seconds.
callouts.comment: The driver's position after a completed lap, in one of three shapes: an invalidated qualifying lap says "That lap didn't count", then "We're currently" and the position; a lap that put the driver on pole says the pole line alone; every other lap says the intro ("That puts us to" for a gain in qualifying, "We're currently" otherwise, and always in a race) and the position, read live in a race. Practice stays silent, and a race hold is left to the race-status update.
callouts.test: Harness → Position → Improved 5 → 3, Worsened 3 → 5, First Valid Lap P1, Qualifying P1 (pole), Holding P1 (qualifying, slow lap), Unchanged P5 (non-PB lap) or the Invalid lap, … buttons (all qualifying). The race branch is mute in the harness (no live position) — In-sim: complete a race lap having gained or lost a place.

callouts.description: You pick up an incident on a counted flying lap of a qualifying session, at the first incident of that lap.
callouts.comment: An incident on a counted qualifying lap: the invalidated line always, then — only in lap-limited qualifying, where a count means something — a tail for how many counted laps remain: out of laps, one to five by count (each a whole sentence with its own encouragement), or plenty above five. The tail is a whole clause, so an if with no else is right for it; a count the case has no key for says nothing. One callout per lap however many incidents; silent on out-laps and beyond the counted attempts.
callouts.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Qualifying Invalidation → Off-Track — 3 laps left (Contact-Car — 1 lap left, Off-Track — out of laps, Off-Track — plenty of laps, Off-Track — time-limited for the other tails; the four (silent) buttons and Same Lap Again (latch) for the suppressions). In-sim: go off track on a flying lap of a lap-limited qualifying session.

callouts.description: You take the checkered flag and cross the line in a race, and your final position (your class position in a multi-class race) is known.
callouts.comment: The final result as the driver crosses the line after the checkered: the driver's name, then one line per result — we won, second place, the podium in third, or the race-is-over line with the position number for fourth or worse. The greeting is optional because names are a union across voices and the result reads whole without it; the position number is part of the last line and stays required. Deferred behind a same-lap best-lap readout rather than cutting it — the race is over either way.
callouts.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Race → Race over — P1 (we won!), or Race over — P2 (second place), Race over — P3 (podium) and Race over — P9 (mid-pack) for the other branches, Race over — multi-class P15 / class P1 for a class win. In-sim: take the checkered flag in a race and cross the line.

callouts.description: A race session begins and three seconds pass — a restart on the pre-green grid included, but not when iRaceDeck connects to a race already under way.
callouts.comment: The grid brief a few seconds into a race session: the driver's name, the starting position (from pole, or qualifying put us to P N), the track and air temperatures, the track wetness, and a setup nudge when the loaded setup looks like a qualifying one. Every clause but the wetness is optional because each is a whole clause the brief reads true without — a name, a position number or a temperature the voice cannot say drops its own clause and nothing else; the position branch is a case inside its clause so a pack can rephrase pole and composed apart. The wetness intro and state are required: the brief always ends on the track.
callouts.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Race Start → Race start — P5, with the race session preset (Race start — P1 (pole), Race start — P65 (out of range) and Race start — no position for the other position branches; the setup nudge has no harness route — In-sim: load a setup whose name matches the qualifying pattern under Setup Warning Patterns). In-sim: sit through the transition into a race session; the brief comes about three seconds in.

callouts.description: Three laps pass in a race without your position changing, and every three laps after that — never on the final lap, and not within twenty seconds of another position readout.
callouts.comment: The every-three-laps status update while the driver holds position in a race: the leader hears the whole still-leading line (still leading our class in a multi-class race), everyone else hears "we're currently" and the live position. Both branches are read at speak time, so a deferred update is never stale. The number is part of the sentence and stays required.
callouts.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Race → Status update (P5 on lap 7) or Leader status (P1 on lap 6) — both are MUTE in the harness, which has no live position for the readout to speak, so only the fire attempt shows in the log. In-sim: hold the same race position for three consecutive laps after the green; the update comes as you cross the line on the third.

callouts.description: The pace car pulls away from the grid to lead the formation lap of a rolling-start race, with you live in the car.
callouts.comment: The pace car has started moving the field onto the formation lap of a rolling start — get up to pace and close the gap. Race-only and live in the car; one of five takes.
callouts.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Rolling Start → Pace car moving, with the race session preset and the on-grid telemetry preset (live in the car). In-sim: sit on the grid of a rolling-start race and wait for the pace car to pull away.

callouts.description: A practice or qualifying session begins and three seconds pass, whether you are in the garage or on track — but not when iRaceDeck connects while you are already out lapping.
callouts.comment: The brief a few seconds into a practice or qualifying session (a race takes the race-start brief instead): the driver's name, which session it is, the pit speed limit with its unit, the track and air temperatures, the track wetness, and — in qualifying only — a setup nudge when the loaded setup looks like a race one. The greeting, the pit-speed limit, both temperatures and the nudge are optional because each is a whole clause the brief reads true without: a name, a limit or a temperature the voice cannot say drops its own clause and nothing else. The session line and the wetness are required — a brief that names no session, or stops at "and the track is", is not a brief.
callouts.test: Harness → Session Start → Fire Session Start, with Session type set to practice or qualifying (race is silent here — it is the race-start callout's); Fire as Fresh Connect covers the mid-session connect. The setup nudge has no harness route — In-sim: in qualifying, load a setup whose name matches the race pattern under Setup Warning Patterns. In-sim: join a practice or qualifying session; the brief comes about three seconds after the session begins, in the garage or on track.

callouts.description: The cars alongside you change — one arrives, a second joins it, one of two drops away, or they swap sides — in any session but Lone Qualify, while you are not on pit road.
callouts.comment: A spotter transition call — a car has appeared alongside, a second one joined it, one of two has gone, or the sides swapped: "Car left", "Two cars right", "Three wide", "Clear right, car left", with inside/outside terms on an oval. The spotter engine picks the clip for the exact transition and hands it over as the spotterClip var, so the call is that one step; it cuts anything in flight and is never replayed late. No radio frame: the beeps would drown a call that has to land at once.
callouts.test: Harness → Radar → Left, Right, Both Sides, Two Left, Two Right (each from the state the button names). In-sim: let a car pull alongside in any session with the spotter enabled.

callouts.description: The last car alongside has truly separated after the radar reads clear, or a car is still alongside when the reminder interval (default three seconds) is due; never in Lone Qualify or on pit road.
callouts.comment: The spotter's informational lines — "Clear" once the car alongside has genuinely separated, and the still-there reminder ("Still there", "Hold your line") on its cadence while a car stays alongside. The same engine-picked spotterClip step as the call, at a lower weight so a reminder can never chop a critical line. No radio frame.
callouts.test: Harness → Radar → Clear (after Left or Right); the still-there reminder repeats on its own while a side stays occupied. In-sim: hold a car alongside for a few seconds, then let it go.

callouts.description: The pre-start countdown of a standing-start race passes ten seconds to go, whether you are in the car or still in the garage.
callouts.comment: Ten seconds to the start — the last mark before the gantry lights.
callouts.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Start → Countdown 10, with the race session preset. In-sim: the pre-start countdown passes ten seconds.

callouts.description: The pre-start countdown of a standing-start race passes thirty seconds to go, whether you are in the car or still in the garage.
callouts.comment: Thirty seconds to the start.
callouts.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Start → Countdown 30, with the race session preset. In-sim: the pre-start countdown passes thirty seconds.

callouts.description: The pre-start countdown of a standing-start race passes sixty seconds to go, whether you are in the car or still in the garage.
callouts.comment: Sixty seconds to the start — the same reminder, one mark closer.
callouts.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Start → Countdown 60, with the race session preset. In-sim: the pre-start countdown passes sixty seconds.

callouts.description: The pre-start countdown of a standing-start race passes ninety seconds to go, whether you are in the car or still in the garage.
callouts.comment: Ninety seconds to the start — the first get-in-the-car reminder, spoken from the garage or session screen too. Ordinary weight, and dropped rather than replayed stale if the bus is busy.
callouts.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Start → Countdown 90, with the race session preset. In-sim: sit in the garage as a standing-start race counts down.

callouts.description: The start lights go out at a standing-start race and the field is released, with you live in the car.
callouts.comment: Lights out — go, go, go. Critical and interrupting: it cuts anything in flight, including a ready line still playing.
callouts.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Start → Go, with the race session preset and the on-grid telemetry preset (live in the car). In-sim: the lights go out at a standing start.

callouts.description: The start lights come on over the grid of a standing-start race while you sit live in the car.
callouts.comment: The start gantry has lit — lights are up, the standing start is seconds away. Critical and interrupting, and replayed rather than lost if a spotter call holds the bus; a later go line replaces it if it never got out.
callouts.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Start → Ready, with the race session preset and the on-grid telemetry preset (live in the car). In-sim: the red lights come on for a standing start.

callouts.description: You switch the tires for your next pit stop to the dry compound.
callouts.comment: The compound for the next stop switched to dry. The one confirmation for the switch — the all-four-tires event iRacing raises alongside it is suppressed before it reaches the engineer.
callouts.test: Harness → Tire Service → Compound → DRY, outside the pit-action cooldown. In-sim: switch the pit-service compound to dry.

callouts.description: You switch the tires for your next pit stop to the wet compound.
callouts.comment: The compound for the next stop switched to wet.
callouts.test: Harness → Tire Service → Compound → WET, outside the pit-action cooldown. In-sim: switch the pit-service compound to wet.

callouts.description: Your tire selection for the next pit stop settles on no tires at all.
callouts.comment: Every tire cleared from the next stop — spoken only when the resulting set is empty, never on a side-switch that merely removes some tires.
callouts.test: Harness → Tire Service → Skip, outside the pit-action cooldown. In-sim: clear every tire in the pit black box.

callouts.description: Your tire selection for the next pit stop settles on all four tires.
callouts.comment: All four tires queued — acknowledgment, then the confirmation. Each tire line answers the RESULTING set, whichever buttons got the driver there.
callouts.test: Harness → Tire Service → All, outside the pit-action cooldown. In-sim: select all four tires in the pit black box.

callouts.description: Your tire selection for the next pit stop settles on the two front tires only.
callouts.comment: Both fronts queued.
callouts.test: Harness → Tire Service → Fronts, outside the pit-action cooldown. In-sim: select the front tires only.

callouts.description: Your tire selection for the next pit stop settles on the two left-side tires only.
callouts.comment: Both left-side tires queued.
callouts.test: Harness → Tire Service → Lefts, outside the pit-action cooldown. In-sim: select the left-side tires only.

callouts.description: Your tire selection for the next pit stop settles on the left-front tire alone.
callouts.comment: The left-front only — a puncture-style single change.
callouts.test: Harness → Tire Service → LF only, outside the pit-action cooldown. In-sim: select only the left-front tire.

callouts.description: Your tire selection for the next pit stop settles on the left-front and right-rear diagonal.
callouts.comment: The left-front and right-rear diagonal.
callouts.test: Harness → Tire Service → LF + RR, outside the pit-action cooldown. In-sim: select the left-front and right-rear tires.

callouts.description: Your tire selection for the next pit stop settles on the left-rear tire alone.
callouts.comment: The left-rear only.
callouts.test: Harness → Tire Service → LR only, outside the pit-action cooldown. In-sim: select only the left-rear tire.

callouts.description: Your tire selection for the next pit stop settles on the two rear tires only.
callouts.comment: Both rears queued.
callouts.test: Harness → Tire Service → Rears, outside the pit-action cooldown. In-sim: select the rear tires only.

callouts.description: Your tire selection for the next pit stop settles on the right-front tire alone.
callouts.comment: The right-front only.
callouts.test: Harness → Tire Service → RF only, outside the pit-action cooldown. In-sim: select only the right-front tire.

callouts.description: Your tire selection for the next pit stop settles on the right-front and left-rear diagonal.
callouts.comment: The right-front and left-rear diagonal.
callouts.test: Harness → Tire Service → RF + LR, outside the pit-action cooldown. In-sim: select the right-front and left-rear tires.

callouts.description: Your tire selection for the next pit stop settles on the two right-side tires only.
callouts.comment: Both right-side tires queued.
callouts.test: Harness → Tire Service → Rights, outside the pit-action cooldown. In-sim: select the right-side tires only.

callouts.description: Your tire selection for the next pit stop settles on the right-rear tire alone.
callouts.comment: The right-rear only.
callouts.test: Harness → Tire Service → RR only, outside the pit-action cooldown. In-sim: select only the right-rear tire.

callouts.description: Your tire selection for the next pit stop settles on every tire but the left-front.
callouts.comment: Three corners — everything but the left-front.
callouts.test: Harness → Tire Service → All except LF, outside the pit-action cooldown. In-sim: select all tires but the left-front.

callouts.description: Your tire selection for the next pit stop settles on every tire but the left-rear.
callouts.comment: Three corners — everything but the left-rear.
callouts.test: Harness → Tire Service → All except LR, outside the pit-action cooldown. In-sim: select all tires but the left-rear.

callouts.description: Your tire selection for the next pit stop settles on every tire but the right-front.
callouts.comment: Three corners — everything but the right-front.
callouts.test: Harness → Tire Service → All except RF, outside the pit-action cooldown. In-sim: select all tires but the right-front.

callouts.description: Your tire selection for the next pit stop settles on every tire but the right-rear.
callouts.comment: Three corners — everything but the right-rear.
callouts.test: Harness → Tire Service → All except RR, outside the pit-action cooldown. In-sim: select all tires but the right-rear.

callouts.description: You take the fast repair off your next pit stop.
callouts.comment: The fast repair removed from the next stop.
callouts.test: Harness → Pit Service → Fast Repair OFF, outside the pit-action cooldown. In-sim: clear the fast-repair toggle in the pit black box.

callouts.description: You add a fast repair to your next pit stop.
callouts.comment: A fast repair queued for the next stop.
callouts.test: Harness → Pit Service → Fast Repair ON, outside the pit-action cooldown. In-sim: press the fast-repair toggle in the pit black box.

callouts.description: You take fuel off the service for your next pit stop.
callouts.comment: The driver removed fuel from the next stop — acknowledgment, then the confirmation.
callouts.test: Harness → Pit Service → Fuel OFF, outside the pit-action cooldown. In-sim: clear the fuel toggle in the pit black box.

callouts.description: You add fuel to the service for your next pit stop.
callouts.comment: The driver queued fuel for the next stop — a short acknowledgment (got it / roger that / copy that) then the confirmation, the shape every toggle confirmation in this family shares. The acknowledgment is pit-actions/acknowledgment, a different pool from the generic acknowledgment/acknowledgment: a smaller set tuned for this register, with its own no-repeat tracker by virtue of being a different group and base, so no named pool is needed for the two to stay independent. Silent for a few seconds after leaving the pit lane, when the sim resets the queue on its own.
callouts.test: Harness → Pit Service → Fuel ON, not within about 4.5 s of Exited Pit Lane (the pit-action cooldown). In-sim: press the fuel toggle in the pit black box, or on a Fuel Service key.

callouts.description: You take the windshield clean off your next pit stop.
callouts.comment: The windshield clean removed from the next stop.
callouts.test: Harness → Pit Service → Windshield OFF, outside the pit-action cooldown. In-sim: clear the windshield toggle in the pit black box.

callouts.description: You add a windshield clean to your next pit stop.
callouts.comment: A windshield clean queued for the next stop.
callouts.test: Harness → Pit Service → Windshield ON, outside the pit-action cooldown. In-sim: press the windshield toggle in the pit black box.

callouts.description: The track's wetness falls to dry from any wetter state.
callouts.comment: The track is fully dry again — the end of a drying trend, and the driest state the sim reports. Only the drying direction takes this line.
callouts.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Track Conditions — Drying → Dry. In-sim: a mostly dry track finishes drying.

callouts.description: The track's wetness falls to lightly wet from any wetter state.
callouts.comment: The track has dried back to lightly wet — the crossover window where slicks come back into the conversation.
callouts.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Track Conditions — Drying → Lightly Wet. In-sim: a moderately wet track keeps drying.

callouts.description: The track's wetness falls to moderately wet from any wetter state.
callouts.comment: The track has dried back to moderately wet — standing water is draining and a line is starting to appear.
callouts.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Track Conditions — Drying → Moderately Wet. In-sim: a very wet track drying after the rain stops.

callouts.description: The track's wetness falls to mostly dry from any wetter state.
callouts.comment: The track has dried back to mostly dry — damp patches off the line, dry grip on it.
callouts.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Track Conditions — Drying → Mostly Dry. In-sim: a very lightly wet track keeps drying.

callouts.description: The track's wetness falls to very lightly wet from any wetter state.
callouts.comment: The track has dried back to very lightly wet — nearly there, a dry line is forming.
callouts.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Track Conditions — Drying → Very Lightly Wet. In-sim: a lightly wet track keeps drying.

callouts.description: The track's wetness falls to very wet from extremely wet.
callouts.comment: The track has dried back to very wet from extremely wet — the first step of a drying trend.
callouts.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Track Conditions — Drying → Very Wet. In-sim: the rain eases on an extremely wet track.

callouts.description: The track's wetness rises to extremely wet from any drier state.
callouts.comment: The track is now extremely wet — the wettest state the sim reports, and the most urgent of the worsening lines.
callouts.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Track Conditions — Worsening → Extremely Wet. In-sim: a downpour on a very wet track.

callouts.description: The track's wetness rises to lightly wet from any drier state.
callouts.comment: The track is now lightly wet and getting wetter — the point where wet tires start to be a question.
callouts.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Track Conditions — Worsening → Lightly Wet. In-sim: steady rain on a very lightly wet track.

callouts.description: The track's wetness rises to moderately wet from any drier state.
callouts.comment: The track is now moderately wet and getting wetter — standing water is forming and the racing line is losing its grip.
callouts.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Track Conditions — Worsening → Moderately Wet. In-sim: heavier rain on a lightly wet track.

callouts.description: The track's wetness rises to mostly dry from dry.
callouts.comment: The track has gone from dry to mostly dry — the first hint of moisture, worth a heads-up before grip goes. Only the worsening direction takes this line; a rapid further step replaces it mid-sentence.
callouts.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Track Conditions — Worsening → Mostly Dry. In-sim: rain starts falling on a dry track in a dynamic-weather session.

callouts.description: The track's wetness rises to very lightly wet from any drier state.
callouts.comment: The track is now very lightly wet and getting wetter — a damp surface with real grip still available.
callouts.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Track Conditions — Worsening → Very Lightly Wet. In-sim: light rain keeps falling on a mostly dry track.

callouts.description: The track's wetness rises to very wet from any drier state.
callouts.comment: The track is now very wet and getting wetter — aquaplaning territory, a warning to back off.
callouts.test: Harness → Scenario Shortcuts → Track Conditions — Worsening → Very Wet. In-sim: heavy rain on a moderately wet track.

vars.name: cornerName.clip
vars.description: The name of the corner the driver is approaching, drawn from the corner-names group (one clip per corner, named by its slug — corner-names/eau-rouge, corner-names/turn-5). Nothing when the voice has no clip for that corner, which skips the callout rather than half-saying it.

vars.name: gap.decimal
vars.description: The tenths of the live gap, 0–9, drawn from the lap-time-decimal group (lap-time-decimal/6 is "point six seconds"). Read live at speak time; nothing when gap.readoutIntro has nothing.

vars.name: gap.line
vars.description: The trend line for the gap that just changed, drawn from the gap group by side and direction: gap/ahead-closing, gap/ahead-opening, gap/behind-closing, gap/behind-opening. A complete sentence on its own.

vars.name: gap.readoutIntro
vars.description: The lead-in of the live gap readout ("Gap is"), from gap/readout-intro. Resolves only when the gap can be read at speak time — under a minute, on the same lap, and still to the car the line named — and gap.second and gap.decimal resolve on exactly the same test, so the three are spoken together or not at all.

vars.name: gap.second
vars.description: The whole seconds of the live gap, 0–59, drawn from the lap-time-second group (lap-time-second/1 is "one"). Read live at speak time; nothing when gap.readoutIntro has nothing.

vars.name: gap.thresholdLine
vars.description: The line for a gap that just dropped under the driver's alert threshold, drawn from the gap group by side: gap/threshold-ahead (we have caught the car ahead) or gap/threshold-behind (the car behind is right with us). A complete sentence on its own.

vars.name: incident.points
vars.description: The penalty points the incident cost, as the sim scored it, spoken as a whole clause from the incidents group (incidents/points-2 is "That cost us two penalty points."). Nothing for a light contact worth no points, or for a count the voice has no clip for — a whole clause, so a script may make it optional and the type line still stands on its own.

vars.name: lapTime.decimal
vars.description: The tenths of a second (0 to 9), spoken as "point N seconds" — the clip that ends the readout. Draws from the lap-time-decimal clip group.

vars.name: lapTime.intro
vars.description: The opening line of the lap-time readout: first-good-lap on the driver's first valid lap of the session, best-lap-yet on every later improvement. Draws from the lap-time-intro clip group.

vars.name: lapTime.minute
vars.description: The whole-minute part of the lap time, as one clip per minute value; nothing for a lap under a minute. Draws from the lap-time-minute clip group — a minute the voice has no clip for aborts the readout.

vars.name: lapTime.second
vars.description: The whole-second part of the lap time (0 to 59), one clip per value with a trailing comma. Draws from the lap-time-second clip group.

vars.name: opponentFlag.number
vars.description: The flagged car's race position as a spoken number, drawn from the position-number group (position-number/4 is "P4"). Read live at speak time — class position in a multi-class race — and falling back to the position the event carried. Only the ahead lines name a position; part of the sentence, so a number that cannot be resolved skips the whole line rather than leaving a gap.

vars.name: opponentPit.number
vars.description: The pitting car's race position as a spoken number, drawn from the position-number group (position-number/4 is "P4"). Read live at speak time — class position in a multi-class race — and falling back to the position the event carried. Part of the sentence, so a number that cannot be resolved skips the whole line rather than leaving a gap.

vars.name: overtake.lost.comeOn
vars.description: The "Come on, <name>." opener of the lost-position line, a full clip per driver name from the position-overtake-come-on group (position-overtake-come-on/driver is the generic fallback). A complete sentence on its own, so the bundled script makes it optional: a voice without the chosen name's clip skips it and the line still plays.

vars.name: pitSpeed.limitIntro
vars.description: The lead-in to the spoken pit-speed limit ("The pit speed limit is"), from the session-start/pit-speed-intro clip. Nothing to say while the session conditions are unknown, so keep it in one optional clause with the number and the unit.

vars.name: pitSpeed.limitNumber
vars.description: The pit-speed limit as a number, from the session-start-speed-numbers/<limit> clip. The group covers the limits iRacing actually uses rather than every number, so a limit the voice has no clip for empties the clause instead of rounding to a wrong one.

vars.name: pitSpeed.limitUnit
vars.description: The pit-speed limit's unit, sentence-final, from the pit-limiter/unit-kmh or pit-limiter/unit-mph clip — recorded apart from the session brief's unit clips, which end on a comma because a temperature follows them there.

vars.name: position.intro
vars.description: The lead-in of a position readout, chosen by what the lap did: position-intro-better/that-puts-us-to for a gain (or a first fix) in qualifying, position-intro-worse/currently for a loss, a held place, or any lap in a race, where standings do not follow from lap times. A fragment of the sentence — keep it required before position.number.

vars.name: position.number
vars.description: The driver's position as a spoken number, drawn from the position-number group (position-number/4 is "P4"): the position the lap just completed left the driver in during qualifying, and the live position at the moment it is spoken during a race — class position in a multi-class session either way. The point of the readout, so a script keeps it required.

vars.name: position.pole
vars.description: The self-contained pole line, position-intro-pole/that-puts-us-on-pole ("That puts us on pole.") — a complete sentence that replaces the intro and the number when the lap put the driver on pole in qualifying.

vars.name: positionReadout.intro
vars.description: The "We're currently" lead-in of a position readout, from position-intro-worse/currently. Resolves to nothing for a second readout within 30 seconds of the last one that moved at most one place — the number is then spoken bare — so the bundled script wraps it in an optional clause; a script that wants the lead-in every time drops the optional. Resolving it also records this readout for the next one's decision, so name it at most once per entry.

vars.name: positionReadout.number
vars.description: The driver's current race position as a spoken number, drawn from the position-number group (position-number/4 is "P4"), read live at the moment it is spoken — class position in a multi-class race. The whole point of the readout, so a script keeps it required.

vars.name: raceEnd.greeting
vars.description: The driver's name as a race-end greeting, one clip per name the voice recorded (the generic driver clip when no name is picked). Draws from the race-end-greeting clip group — a name the voice lacks resolves to nothing, so keep it optional.

vars.name: raceEnd.podiumThird
vars.description: The whole third-place line — we made the podium. Draws the podium-third line from the race-end clip group.

vars.name: raceEnd.position
vars.description: The final position as a spoken number — the class position in a multi-class race, the overall position otherwise. Draws from the position-number clip group; a position the voice has no clip for aborts the readout.

vars.name: raceEnd.raceOverResultIs
vars.description: The lead-in of the fourth-or-worse readout — the race is over, the final result for us is. A fragment of a sentence: the position number must follow it. Draws the race-over-result-is line from the race-end clip group.

vars.name: raceEnd.secondPlace
vars.description: The whole second-place line. Draws the second-place line from the race-end clip group.

vars.name: raceEnd.weWon
vars.description: The whole winning line — we won, well done. Draws the we-won line from the race-end clip group.

vars.name: raceStart.airTempNumber
vars.description: The air temperature as a whole number in the driver's display unit. Draws from the session-start-temp-numbers clip group; a reading outside the recorded range aborts the clause it sits in.

vars.name: raceStart.degreesUnit
vars.description: The temperature unit word — degrees celsius or degrees fahrenheit, per the driver's display setting. Draws the degrees-celsius and degrees-fahrenheit lines from the session-start clip group.

vars.name: raceStart.greeting
vars.description: The race-start greeting with the driver's name — "time to race, <name>" as one clip per name the voice recorded (the generic driver clip when no name is picked). Draws from the race-start-greeting clip group; a name the voice lacks resolves to nothing, so keep it optional.

vars.name: raceStart.position
vars.description: The grid position as a spoken number. Draws from the position-number clip group; a position the voice has no clip for resolves to nothing and aborts the clause it sits in.

vars.name: raceStart.trackTempNumber
vars.description: The track temperature as a whole number in the driver's display unit. Draws from the session-start-temp-numbers clip group; a reading outside the recorded range aborts the clause it sits in.

vars.name: raceStart.wetness
vars.description: The track wetness state as a word — dry, mostly dry, very lightly wet, lightly wet, moderately wet, very wet or extremely wet. Draws the wetness-<state> lines from the session-start clip group.

vars.name: raceStatus.intro
